sections.title: An optimal constant for vector balancing with permutations
sections.abstract: The authors introduce vector balancing with independent sign and coordinate-permutation choices, prove explicit bounds for the total and prefix problems, and show the leading asymptotic constant is optimal in dimension.
sections.claimed_result: For vectors in the Euclidean unit ball of R^n, the authors give a bound of (sqrt(n-1)+1)/sqrt(n) on the maximum l-infinity norm of every signed/permuted prefix sum; the asymptotic leading constant is optimal.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Finite sequence of vectors in the Euclidean unit ball B_2^n; each may be signed and have its coordinates permuted. The bound controls every prefix sum in l-infinity.
sections.unique_caveat: The coordinate-permutation freedom is part of the problem; this is not an ordinary sign-only vector balancing result.
sections.ranking_evidence: Wolfram MathWorld's vector-balancing entry cites this specific preprint and summarizes the asymptotically sharp result, an unusually prompt independent reference; not a readership measure.

sections.title: Linear circumference in vertex-transitive graphs
sections.abstract: Every finite connected vertex-transitive graph on at least three vertices contains a cycle of length at least a fixed positive fraction of its number of vertices, with a stronger near-spanning bound at sufficiently large degree.
sections.claimed_result: The authors prove a cycle of length at least c n for absolute c>0; at sufficiently large degree d, a cycle of length at least (1-d^(-1/100))n.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Finite, connected, vertex-transitive graphs on n≥3 vertices; the stronger bound requires sufficiently large degree.
sections.unique_caveat: A linear-size cycle need not be Hamiltonian; the Lovász Hamiltonicity conjecture remains open.
sections.ranking_evidence: Concrete advance on the Lovász Hamiltonicity problem, with a separate mathematical review appearing in the same short window.

sections.title: The critical Ising magnetization field can be reconstructed from its +/- interfaces
sections.abstract: For critical Ising models on planar lattice approximations, the authors prove that the continuum magnetization field is a measurable function of the nested CLE_3 limit of spin interfaces.
sections.claimed_result: Measurability of the critical Ising magnetization field from nested CLE_3 interfaces, with a consistency consequence for construction through colored CLE_16/3.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Scaling limits of critical planar Ising models; the principal setup in the introduction uses sufficiently regular planar domains and plus boundary conditions.
sections.unique_caveat: The reverse measurability direction is conjectured, not proved; the authors also explain why direct Minkowski-content recovery does not apply.
sections.ranking_evidence: The arXiv mathematics/probability account highlighted the preprint; the authors note the main results were announced in June 2025. This is a limited visibility signal, not evidence of broad readership.

sections.title: Baernstein's quasi-norm monotonicity conjecture for polynomials with unimodular zeros
sections.abstract: For every nonzero degree-n polynomial whose zeros lie on the unit circle, the ratio of its L^r size to that of 1+z^n is nondecreasing in r, including endpoint conventions r=0 and r=∞.
sections.claimed_result: The author proves Baernstein's normalized quasi-norm monotonicity conjecture and derives consequences including an L^r extension of Visser's coefficient inequality and sharp related inequalities.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Nonzero complex polynomials of degree n with all zeros on the unit circle; comparison against Q_n(z)=1+z^n for 0≤s≤t≤∞.
sections.unique_caveat: The theorem assumes all zeros are unimodular and does not cover arbitrary polynomials. This is a new preprint claim, not a peer-reviewed assessment here.
sections.ranking_evidence: The abstract states a resolution of a named conjecture and reports a Lean 4 formalization; concrete mathematical/formal-verification signals, not independent citation momentum.

sections.title: Generic solutions to symmetric linear equations
sections.abstract: The authors strengthen a result of Ruzsa by finding equal-sum k-tuples in dense subsets with no other subset-sum coincidence, then extend related bounds to finite Abelian groups and representable matroids.
sections.claimed_result: For fixed k≥2 and |A|≥C N^(1/k), the authors obtain 2k distinct elements with equal k-sums and only that one subset-sum coincidence; related finite-field matroid extremal bounds are also proved.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The density threshold uses a constant depending on fixed k; the group extension is strongest for odd-order finite Abelian groups, with a weaker result for even order.
sections.unique_caveat: The even-order group result is explicitly weaker, and the abstract does not claim uniformly sharp constants or extremal behavior.
sections.ranking_evidence: The abstract spans additive combinatorics, finite Abelian groups, and matroid extremal bounds, providing cross-problem reach; no independent citation-momentum signal was established at this age.

sections.title: Linear arboricity conjecture for infinite graphs
sections.abstract: The authors extend the linear-arboricity conjecture to infinite graphs of finite maximum degree, prove equivalence of the finite and infinite versions, and introduce a topological variant.
sections.claimed_result: Finite and infinite versions are equivalent; topological linear arboricity differs from linear arboricity by at most one; each 2k-regular graph of girth at least 2k has topological linear arboricity at most k+1.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The infinite-graph extension assumes finite maximum degree; the final bound assumes 2k-regularity and girth at least 2k.
sections.unique_caveat: The equivalence transfers the underlying conjecture between finite and infinite settings rather than proving its conjectured bound.
sections.ranking_evidence: The paper supplies an explicit equivalence between finite and infinite formulations and a separate regular-graph bound; inclusion is based on these structural results rather than measured popularity.
